bull.b: Debt of about $0.6M against $56.0M of equity indicates limited leverage and a relatively conservative capital structure. This reduces near-term solvency and interest burden risk, preserving flexibility to direct available resources toward clinical development while financing needs remain high.

Australian ethics approval and regulatory clearance move EQ504 into a controlled Phase 1 study with planned early-November dosing. Its safety, pharmacokinetic and tissue-biomarker design can generate target-validation data that improves later-stage development decisions and partnering credibility.

Itolizumab gives Equillium an identified lead asset with a differentiated CD6 mechanism intended to modulate T-cell activation and inflammatory signaling. Development across aGVHD, lupus nephritis and other immune-mediated diseases provides multiple clinical avenues for the platform to demonstrate value.

bear.b: TTM revenue is zero and net loss is about $18.0M, following $41.1M of revenue and an $8.1M loss in 2024. This reversal shows commercial contribution is not yet durable and leaves results dependent on clinical progress rather than recurring operating income.

Operating cash flow of about -$20.0M and free cash flow of about -$20.1M remain similar to recent years. Persistent burn means clinical programs consume cash without internally generated funding, increasing reliance on external capital to sustain development.

Negative ROE of roughly -0.41 indicates continuing equity erosion while losses persist. Even with low debt, repeated deficits can shrink the capital base and reduce financial flexibility, making successful clinical execution and future funding access increasingly important.
